version: 3.0, 7 November 2026 (from the Master Training Manual, Appendix H and I)
intro: How every part of the Archē broker portal works, what to do when something goes wrong, and how to get the most out of it. The same guide is in the portal under Help and in the academy as Systems training.

features.title: Joining, roles and access
features.purpose: Only approved people can use the portal, and each person sees only what their role needs.
steps: Open the portal address and sign in with the email you were invited with: Sign in with Microsoft, Email me a sign-in link, or your password if you set one. Forgot password? sends a link to set a new one.
First time: fill in Join with your full legal name as on your contract, the country you work from and your academy completion code, and tick the portal agreement.
Wait for approval. The Director approves every broker before the first enquiry.

Your role decides what you see: brokers see their own trips, leads and commission; the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, sees every trip and the Authorisation queue; the Director sees everything.
trouble: The portal will not sign me in
Use the email address your invitation went to. A sign-in link works once and only for a short time: ask for a new one. Still stuck: press Forgot password? or ask the Director.
I am stuck on Request sent
The Director has not approved you yet. Ask the Director; approval needs your contract and academy code.
I see Access ended
Your access was ended. Contact the Director if you think this is a mistake.
I cannot see a trip or lead a colleague mentions
Brokers see only their own trips and leads. Ask the Director.
tips: Always sign in with the email you were invited with: your trips, leads and academy progress are tied to it.
Bookmark the portal link on your phone; every page works on a small screen.

Director: Team > Invite someone to join shows where each person is in joining: the step they are on out of nine, the academy modules passed, a progress bar and when they last signed in. Log opens every step with its date, newest first.
try: broker
Open the test version and switch between Test Broker and Test Director in the orange bar: compare the menus.

features.title: Today (brokers and the Director)
features.who: Brokers; the Director, or a person the Director has mandated
features.purpose: Your opening page, the only start page: every task for today, most urgent first, flights today and tomorrow, what waits on others, then your progress this month and your place in the team.
steps: Read the progress tiles: standard bookings this month, commission earned this month, quote-to-confirmation rate, rank and prospects added against the minimum.
Work Your tasks from the top. Red dots are urgent: an overdue lead, a trip returned at authorisation, a payment due.
Tap a task to open the lead or trip it refers to.
Compare yourself with the team by points, confirmed trips, enquiries, prospects added or follow-up score.
trouble: My rank shows a dash
The leaderboard updates at each assignment round, every 3 hours. It appears after the first round of the month.
Commission shows USD 0 although I have flown trips
Commission counts only trips that have flown and whose client payment has cleared. Ask the Director to record the payment.
A task stays on the list after I did it
Tasks clear when the portal sees the change: log the contact, update the trip or send it for authorisation.
tips: Start every day on Today and clear the red items first.
Overdue leads move to another broker at the next round: a two-minute logged contact keeps the lead yours.
Use the team comparison to see where you lose points; follow-up score is usually the quickest win.
try: broker
As Test Broker, open Today: work Your tasks from the top, then read Progress this month.

features.title: Today (Director)
features.purpose: Everything that needs the Director, on one page, from any device.
steps: Read Your decisions: trips waiting for authorisation, late payments and other red flags, prospects that went cold with three brokers, and join requests.
Restart a cold prospect's rotation, mark it Do not contact, or open it to assign it yourself.
Check Prospect rotation: last round, what moved and the figures per broker. Use Preview to see the next round, Run now to run it.
Check Running in the background: sanctions screen, prospect rotation, research agent and nightly backup.
Use the analytics: gross profit from trips flown over six months, this month's funnel and confirmed trips by broker.
trouble: A background job shows not run yet or an old date
The jobs run on GitHub (Portal jobs). It runs again at its next time; if it is late twice, open the job's run on GitHub and read the error.
Run now does nothing
Another round may be running. Wait a minute and reload.
tips: Open Today once a day: anything late or waiting for you is at the top.
A prospect that went cold three times is often a wrong-fit organisation: consider Do not contact rather than another rotation.

features.title: New enquiry and airport search
features.purpose: Capture the trip once, correctly, with the right airports.
steps: Choose New enquiry, or Open an enquiry from a lead.
Enter the client: name, company, email, phone, country of residence and the payer if different.
For each leg type a city, airport name or code (for example London) and pick the airport from the list. The portal stores the ICAO code and shows the airport name.
Add date, local time and passengers per leg, the aircraft category and any notes.
Save. The trip appears under My trips as Enquiry.
trouble: Save says choose the airport from the list
The text typed is not a known airport. Type a city or code and pick one of the suggestions.
The airport I need is not offered

The list holds 7,009 airports suitable for jets. Type the four-letter ICAO code; if it is still missing, ask the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, as the runway may be too short for jets.
Times look wrong
Times are local at the departure airport. Confirm the time zone with the client in writing.
tips: Type the city, not the airport: the list shows every suitable airport nearby, including business-aviation fields such as Biggin Hill or Le Bourget.
Write special requests in the notes: the portal turns many of them into suggested requests and extras.
Open enquiries from leads with Open an enquiry, so the trip is linked to the prospect and counts on the leaderboard.
try: broker
Make a New enquiry: Singapore Seletar to Bangkok Don Mueang, 4 passengers, next month.

features.title: Client requests and operational extras
features.who: Brokers until the trip goes for authorisation; the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, until the confirmation is issued
features.purpose: List every request and every operational need, with how it is charged, so the confirmation is complete and nothing is invoiced by surprise.
steps: Open the trip. Under Client requests and Operational extras charged to the client, read the suggestions.
Tap a suggestion to add it, or Add request / Add extra for your own.
For each line choose the category, describe it, and choose how it is charged: included in the charter price, at cost after the flight, or fixed price.
For a fixed price enter the supplier's written price. The client pays that price divided by 0.91, rounded up; the portal shows it.
Use AI: suggest more for anything the rules or route may need.
trouble: I cannot edit the lines
The trip is with the Director for checking, or confirmed. Ask the Director to change it.
The confirmation says a fixed price is missing
A line set to fixed price has no supplier price. Enter it, or change the line to at cost.
A suggestion does not apply
Ignore it; suggestions are prompts to ask the operator, never facts.
tips: Ask about catering, cars, pets, children, luggage and allergies on the first call: changes later cost time and money.
Winter, night departures, waiting days and international arrivals almost always bring operational extras: confirm them before quoting.
Use fixed price only with a written supplier quote; anything that depends on the day is at cost.
try: broker
Add a client request (a small dog) and an operational extra (de-icing, at cost) to your enquiry.

features.title: Operator quote and price
features.purpose: Record the operator's all-in quote so the portal sets the client price at 9%.
steps: From Avinode, enter the operator's legal name as on its AOC, aircraft type, registration and Avinode trip ID.
Enter the operator all-in price and any direct trip costs not in it (supplier items Archē buys).
Quoted in another currency: choose it; the portal fills in the European Central Bank reference rate of the day and flags a rate more than 3% away from it.
Read the price preview: client price = (operator price + direct costs) ÷ 0.91, rounded up.
Save. The trip moves to Quoted.

When you save, the portal checks in the background: the names against the sanctions lists, the operator against the EU Air Safety List, and a US registration (N…) against the FAA list of aircraft on each operator's charter certificate. Anything that does not match shows in Trip checks with the source and the date.
trouble: The price looks too high or low
Check you entered the all-in operator price, including positioning, and no extras twice.
The Director changed my operator price
The Director, or a person the Director has mandated, confirms the price on Avinode; the confirmed figure is used and the difference is flagged.
tips: Never round down and never quote below 9% without the Director's approval.
Re-confirm availability and price with the operator before the offer expires.
try: broker
Enter an operator price of USD 20,000 and check the client price: 20,000 ÷ 0.91, rounded up, is USD 21,979.

features.title: Documents
features.who: Brokers until the trip goes for authorisation
features.purpose: Keep every document for the trip in one place, never in email.
steps: Open the trip, choose the document type and the file, and select Attach.
Attach the operator quote, AOC, insurance certificate, safety audit evidence and the client's KYC documents.
Open any document from the trip file.
trouble: Attach does nothing
Choose a file first. Large files take a few seconds.
I cannot attach after sending for authorisation
Documents are locked with the trip. Send them to the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, through the portal; they attach them.
tips: Never send passports or contracts by email or chat apps.
Name scanned files clearly before uploading.
try: broker
Attach a small PDF to your trip.

features.title: Pre-issue checks and sending for authorisation
features.purpose: Hand the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, a complete, compliant trip.
steps: The portal sets six of the seven pre-issue checks itself, from the records you complete: never-sell list and trip risk screen from Trip checks (nothing red, every amber confirmed with the operator), AOC from Documents (the operator's AOC attached), safety audit from Operator safety, insurance and operator terms from Operator terms and insurance. You cannot tick them by hand; complete the record and the tick follows, and a new red item takes it back. Only routing and permits (confirmed with the operator) is your own tick.

Fill in Operator safety on the trip: the audit the operator holds, the aircraft type, two pilots, the insurance amount and the five-year history. For an accepted audit, add its expiry date, the date you checked it in the auditor's registry and the link, and attach the evidence as "Safety audit". For an Archē-approved operator, choose it from the approved-operator list: the portal checks the approval is valid on the last flight date. For any other operator, the Director approves the trip after the checks in 8.3. Your quote and the confirmation show the operator's safety status in one line. The safety-audit tick follows this record.

Complete KYC and save the sanctions screening record. The portal has already screened the client, company, payer and operator (reused from your save if under 48 hours old, otherwise screened when you open the trip): add the passengers, owners of 25% or more and the aircraft owner if not listed, then press Save.
Create the payment request in our payment provider and enter its reference on the trip.
Press Send for authorisation. The button opens only when the trip is complete: the panel Steps to book this trip lists what is still missing and takes you to each field.
trouble: Send for authorisation is greyed out
One of the required items is missing; the note under the button lists them.
The trip came back as Returned
Read the Director's note at the top of the trip, fix it and send again.
tips: Run the AI check before sending; it catches cabotage, permits and missing information.
A trip returned twice costs the client's confidence: complete it the first time.
try: broker
Complete the trip checks, tick KYC, enter a payment request reference and press Send for authorisation.

features.title: Authorisation
features.who: The Director, or a person the Director has mandated
features.purpose: Check, confirm and record every trip that brokers send.
steps: Open Authorisation; take the oldest trip waiting for authorisation.
Confirm the operator price on Avinode, send Request to Book and enter direct trip costs.
Check the KYC and sanctions screening record and the payment request reference the broker recorded.
Save. Approve the booking, then Prepare and issue confirmation; or Return to broker with a note.
trouble: I see a note instead of the Authorisation panel
It is your own trip. Another person the Director has mandated handles it.
The broker's operator price differs from Avinode
Use the Avinode figure; the difference is flagged in Control.
tips: Work the queue oldest first; check it at least twice a day.
Never take payment details by email; every client pays through the payment request.
try: owner
As Test Director, open Authorisation and the trip you sent: see what the authoriser checks, then Return to broker with a note.

features.title: Charter confirmation
features.who: Brokers prepare; the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, issues
features.purpose: Produce the signed contract: booking details, requests and extras, Part A and Part B.
steps: Open Charter confirmation from the trip. Fill in charterer address, KYC reference, lead passenger, aircraft year and seats, operator AOC and authority, signatory.
Read the live checks on the right: fix every red item and every missing field.
Use AI check for a second look.
The Director issues it: the portal assigns the reference, saves the PDF to the trip and locks it.
A change after issue: Prepare revision, then Issue revision n.
trouble: Issue is greyed out
A required field or check is missing; the list shows which.
Company details are missing
The Director must fill in Settings > Company details once.
The PDF did not save
Download it from the confirmation screen and attach it to the trip.
tips: Fill the confirmation while the broker still has the details fresh; drafts save automatically.
The deposit is 25% of the charter price (at least USD 2,500); fixed extras are paid with the balance 7 days before departure.
try: owner
As Test Director, approve the trip and prepare the confirmation. Then switch to Test Broker and read its status.

features.title: Payments, flight and commission
features.who: The Director, or a person the Director has mandated, records; everyone sees their own commission
features.purpose: Record money and flights so commission is right and on time.
steps: The Director records the date the client payment cleared in the payment account.
The Director records the operator payment.
After the last leg, the Director records the flight date.
Commission appears in the month the trip flew, paid by the 15th of the next month; the Director marks it paid.
trouble: My trip flew but no commission
The client payment has not been recorded, or the flight date has not. Ask the Director.
Commission seems low
Commission is a share of gross profit, including the margin on fixed-price extras; at-cost items carry no margin.
tips: Chase unpaid confirmations after 5 days: the Control page flags them.
Record flights the day they happen, so Today stays true.
try: owner
As Test Director, record the client payment and the flight, then switch to Test Broker and see the commission.

features.title: My leads and adding prospects
features.purpose: Work the organisations assigned to you and add the ones you know.
steps: Open My leads. Leads are sorted by when contact is due.
Open a lead, read why them and how to approach, use a contact route, then log the contact with channel, outcome and a note.
Add a prospect: organisation, segment, country, public source link, contact route and why they charter.
Add or correct a contact route on any lead to keep the database current.
Open an enquiry from a lead when the organisation has a trip.
trouble: My new prospect says Being checked
It is checked for duplicates at the next round, within 3 hours.
It says Already known
Another broker added it first; it stays with them. Keep adding new ones.
A lead disappeared
It went cold and moved to another broker, or it was marked Do not contact.
tips: My leads are prospects from research (48 hours for first contact). A client who asks directly, by the website, phone, email or messaging, is an enquiry: contact them within 15 minutes.
Contact new leads the same day: the 48-hour clock starts at assignment.
Every organisation you add earns points and a bigger share of new leads; ten a month is the minimum, not the target.
Anyone who opts out is Do not contact at once, for everyone.
try: broker
As Test Broker, open My leads, open a lead and log a contact with a proper note.

features.title: Prospects database
features.purpose: The global list of organisations, with sources, contact routes and status.
steps: Filter by region, country, province, segment, type and status, or search.
Open a prospect to see why, how to approach, contact routes, source, assignment history and the contact log.
Assign it to a broker, or mark Do not contact.
Add a prospect with its public source.

Research agent (Director): switch it on (it finds new organisations, charter operators, business-jet suppliers at business airports worldwide and, once a week, investors and partners for your private list), choose how often it runs (every day, Monday to Friday or once a week), list the focus areas one per line (empty uses the standard list) and press Save settings. A Claude scheduled task does the research each morning when it is due, with no AI key and no AI bill. Nothing goes in until it passes every check: a public source page that opens and names the organisation, organisations only, not already known, no excluded or sanctioned place, no marketplace or broker site, contacts only as the organisation publishes them on its own site, opt-outs respected, and a sanctions pre-screen. The panel shows the last run, what it added and what the checks rejected, with the reason.
trouble: A prospect has no contact routes
The research agent adds them over time; brokers can add them too.
Status shows Your decision
It went cold with three brokers. Restart the rotation or mark Do not contact.
A prospect shows Your decision with a sanctions flag
The research agent found a possible sanctions match. Check the names against the list before any contact, then clear it or mark Do not contact.
The agent added nothing
It runs only when it is on and due. The panel lists what the checks rejected and why; widen or change the focus areas if most were already known.
tips: Use the region tiles to see where coverage is thin, then add prospects there.
Never store private individuals' details; organisations and roles only.

features.title: Prospect rotation
features.who: Runs automatically; the Director can run it
features.purpose: Give every broker a fair, steady flow of leads and never let a prospect go cold.
steps: Every 3 hours, and when the Director opens the portal, the round imports prospects brokers added, catches duplicates, merges contact updates and assigns free prospects.
Each broker is scored on country and region fit, follow-up record, conversions and fair share; brokers who add prospects get a bigger share.
No first contact within 48 hours, or no follow-up for 14 days, and the lead moves to the next broker with its history. After three brokers it goes to the Director.
Not now leads come back after 90 days to a different broker.
trouble: A broker gets no new leads
They may be at the open-lead limit, have leads going cold, or be below the monthly minimum late in the month.
Rules need changing
The Director changes them in Settings > Prospect assignment and incentives.
tips: Use Preview on Today before changing the rules, to see their effect.
Keep the number of open leads per broker realistic: fewer, worked leads beat many cold ones.

features.title: Points and leaderboard
features.purpose: Make good habits visible and reward them.
steps: Points this month: 3 per organisation added, 1 per lead contacted per day, 1 per contact route added or corrected (up to 20), 10 per enquiry from a lead, 25 per trip flown, minus 3 when a lead goes cold.
See your rank on Today and in My leads.
trouble: Points did not change after I logged a contact
Points update at each round, every 3 hours.
tips: Flown trips are worth the most; but daily contacts and added prospects keep you ahead early in the month.
try: broker
On Today, find your points and your place in the team.

features.title: AI assistant and co-pilot
features.purpose: A second pair of eyes on every trip, and answers to questions about the rules.
steps: On a trip, use the co-pilot: check the trip, draft an email or suggest the next step.
On a lead, use Suggest approach for a first message with an opt-out line.
In Assistant, ask any question about the rules, a trip or an operator.
The Director can write the daily briefing in Control.
trouble: The co-pilot asks for permission
Allow Claude when asked, or in the artifact's Permissions menu.
Too many requests
Wait a minute and try again.
tips: The co-pilot sends the AI the trip facts, never passenger names or contact details. Never type passport, ID or bank numbers, passenger names or private contact details into the Assistant or a trip note (Module 3.7).
Treat AI output as a draft: you are responsible for what you send.
try: broker
Open Assistant to see where questions go. Answers work only in the real portal.

features.title: Control
features.purpose: See signs that business is leaving the portal or that money is late.
steps: Read the flags: unpaid confirmations, old quotes and enquiries, price differences, the same client with two brokers, low quote-to-booking rates.
Open the trip behind a flag and act.
Write today's AI briefing for the outlook, risks and coaching.
trouble: A flag will not clear
Fix the cause: record the payment, update or withdraw the trip.
tips: A broker with many quotes and few confirmations may be booking outside the portal: talk to them early.

features.title: Team and authorisation
features.purpose: Approve people, end access and choose who may authorise trips besides you.
steps: Approve or decline requests to join (Onboarding page), and send the agreement once the qualification checklist is complete.

Invitations (Team): invite a person by name and email; the list shows each one's joining progress and log. Someone quiet for 3 days gets a Remind button: read the email, then Send. Remind all sends the same reminder, each with the person's own next step and a fresh personal link, to everyone who has a login and is not yet on the team. The reminder says that Archē Executive launches in December. Nothing goes out until you press Send; replies come to you.
You authorise every trip by default. In Team, tick May authorise to mandate someone else (never for their own trips), or give supervisor rights; every decision is logged with your name.

When someone leaves, open their file in Onboarding and press End engagement: 30 days' notice, by agreement or for breach. Access ends on the end date, open enquiries go back to the pool and prospects back into rotation.

Client handover (agreement clause 8.5): the leaving file lists the broker's clients from their trips. Name a successor for each and press Hand over. The successor gets the client as an own lead with the trip history and a call due within 48 hours; the leaving broker sees a task to introduce the successor personally before the end date. Tick Introduced when done; the file shows Contacted when the successor logs the first call.
You can take clients yourself: choose Me as the successor, or press Hand all to me.

Lock now (fraud or another ground for ending at once, agreement clause 8.3): press Lock now next to the person in Team, write the reason and confirm. Access ends at once (the database refuses every request from that login), rights and alerts are removed, open enquiries go back to the pool, prospects back into rotation, and all their clients and own leads move to you. Open trips stay with you to finish. No notice goes to members.
Today reminds you of clients not yet handed over, calls overdue and data deletion not confirmed.
trouble: A leaving broker has no clients in the handover list
Their clients come from their trips; leads that never booked go to you automatically.
The successor's call shows overdue
Ask the successor to call today and log it on the lead; reassign if they cannot.
tips: Hand over clients on the day notice is given, not at the end: the leaving broker can still make the personal introduction.
Give each client to a broker who serves the same region or language.

features.title: Reports
features.purpose: Charts for a quick overview and every report to download.
steps: Open Reports. The charts show booked value and gross profit by month, trips by stage, open trips by red, amber and clear trip checks, and gross profit by broker; hover a bar for the details.

Download a report: Trips, Payments, Commission, Compliance (KYC, sanctions screening, trip checks, insurance, audit) or Operator library, as CSV, as one Excel file with every report, or as a print view to save as PDF.
Client email and phone and prospect contact details are never exported. Every download is logged in the access log.

features.title: Settings
features.purpose: Commercial terms, company details, assignment rules and backup.
steps: Terms: margin, standard booking value, commission rates.
Company details: printed on every confirmation; needed before the first issue.
Prospect assignment and incentives: contact times, limits, minimum adds, extra lead share, leaderboard visibility.

Backup: download a full copy at any time; the nightly backup runs by itself: every table and every stored file (documents, registries, the research agent's key, the sanctions index), encrypted and kept 90 days.

AI spend: this month's spend of the portal AI (the Assistant, trip co-pilot, roleplay lab and briefing) against the monthly cap you set here. At the cap the AI pauses until the next month. The research agent uses no AI key and costs nothing here.
trouble: Brokers do not see a rule change
Rules apply from the next round; ask brokers to reload the portal.
tips: Change commercial terms only at the start of a month, so commission stays easy to check.

features.title: Security and access log
features.purpose: Keep the portal ringfenced.
steps: Review who opened the portal and when.
Keep the Share menu to named people: brokers Contributor; never a public link.
trouble: Someone unknown appears in the access log
End their access and remove them from the Share menu at once.
tips: Every screen carries a watermark with the viewer's name: screenshots are traceable.

features.title: Backups
features.purpose: An independent copy of everything in the portal.
steps: Every night at 02:17 Bangkok time the whole database is copied, encrypted with the Director's backup passphrase and kept for 90 days outside the database (GitHub, Portal jobs).
Uploaded documents and issued PDFs stay in the portal's file store.
Settings > Backup: download a full copy at any time, and test a restore with the restore check.
trouble: The nightly backup has not reported
Open Portal jobs on GitHub and read the last backup run; it runs again the next night.
A restore check fails
Use the copy from the night before and tell the Director at once.
tips: Download a full copy before any big change to settings or the team.

features.title: Help and FAQ
features.purpose: Answers in seconds, and a FAQ that grows from real questions.
steps: Open Help. Search the FAQ and the feature guides.
Ask a question: the AI answers at once from the manual and this guide, and your question is saved.
Questions asked often are added to the FAQ automatically, without names or client details. The Director can edit or remove any FAQ entry.
trouble: The AI answer seems wrong
Mark it Not helpful; the Director sees it and corrects the answer.
tips: Search before asking: most answers are already there.
Never put client names or passport details in a question.
try: broker
Open Help and search the guide for a word such as cancellation.

features.title: Flight following
features.who: The trip's broker, who owns the trip to the last landing; the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, records the flight
features.purpose: The broker who owns the trip follows it until the last passenger has landed, so the client hears about a change from us first.
steps: Open the trip. The Flight following panel appears once the confirmation is issued.
For each leg, set Departed, Landed, Delayed, Diverted or Cancelled with the operator's local time and a short note.
Tell the client at once about any delay, diversion or cancellation.
When every leg has landed and the client has paid, the Director presses Last leg landed: record flight. The trip moves to Flown and aftercare opens for the broker.
trouble: The record-flight button does not appear
Every leg must be Landed or Cancelled, and the client payment must be recorded first.
I cannot change a leg
Only the trip's broker and the Director edit leg status.
tips: Take times from the operator's movement message, never estimate.
Keep notes short and factual: the broker reads them before calling the client.
try: broker
On a confirmed trip, set the first leg to Departed with a time and a short note.

features.title: Aftercare, rating and service recovery
features.purpose: The broker who owns the trip calls the client within 24 hours of the last landing, asks for a rating and puts any problem right (manual 11.4).
steps: After the flight, the trip shows an Aftercare panel with a due time and a checklist.
Call or message the client personally, then press Log follow-up with a short note.
Press Email the rating request: your email opens with template B.9 and one-click 1–5 links that reply to the bookings address.
When the client answers, record the rating: overall, aircraft, crew and broker, the comment, and tick the box only if the client agreed in writing that we may quote it.
Any overall score of 3 or less opens Service recovery: call the client within 1 working day, then record what was agreed. The Director is told automatically.
The file closes when payments are settled, the follow-up and rating request are logged, and any recovery and debrief are done.
trouble: Follow-up shows as overdue
More than 24 hours have passed since the last landing. Call the client now and log it.
The client has no email on the trip
Add the address in your email before sending, and add it to the trip next time.
tips: Ratings go into the operator scorecard: they decide which operators we book.
Never publish a rating or comment without the client's written permission, and never write or ask for reviews in exchange for anything.
try: broker
On a flown trip, follow the aftercare steps: log the follow-up and open the rating request.

features.title: Post-trip debrief (supervised bookings)
features.who: Trainees in stage 6, mentors and the Director, or a person the Director has mandated
features.purpose: Each supervised booking is reviewed by trainee, mentor and the Director within 3 working days (manual 14.6, template B.8).
steps: The Director ticks Supervised for the broker in Team.
After each of that broker's flights, the Aftercare panel shows the debrief with three parts.

Each person scores the three measures from 1 to 5: pre-issue checks, extras explained to the client, and client satisfaction, then adds errors found, what went well, what to change and one action, with who does it and by when.
The booking counts towards sign-off only when all three parts are signed. Team shows each broker's count out of 10.
trouble: The debrief does not appear
The broker is not ticked as Supervised in Team, or the trip is not flown yet.
tips: Be specific: one clear action is worth more than a long list.
try: broker
Read the debrief steps; they apply to your supervised bookings.

features.title: Roleplay lab
features.who: Everyone in training; the Director sees the team summary
features.purpose: Practise difficult calls out loud with an AI client, assistant, family-office manager or operator, and get scored on the lab sheet (manual 14.4–14.5).
steps: Open Training, then Roleplay lab.
Choose one of the 12 scenarios or describe your own, who you speak to and the level.
Press Start the call. Type, or press Speak and say your part; the other side answers in writing.
Press End and score. You get a score out of 100, the moments that cost points and a model answer. Sessions are saved to your record.
trouble: Speak does not appear
Your browser does not support speech input. Type instead; Chrome and Edge support it.
The AI is busy
Wait a minute and try again.
tips: Never use real client names in practice.
The AI score is for practice. Certification is decided by the Director's scored lab.
try: broker

features.title: The rules behind every booking
features.purpose: The business rules the portal enforces. Know them before your first enquiry.
steps: Everything is enquired, quoted, booked and paid in the portal, and nowhere else. All figures are in USD.
Client price = (operator price + direct trip costs) ÷ 0.91, rounded up: Archē keeps 9% of what the client pays. A different margin only by the Director's decision, with the reason recorded.
Deposit 25% of the charter price, at least USD 2,500, on signature; the balance 7 days before the first departure; full payment at once if departure is less than 7 days away.
Fixed-price extras go on the balance. Items at cost are invoiced after the flight with receipts, without margin.
Clients pay only through a payment request. Never print, store or send bank details.
The Director, or a person the Director has mandated, authorises every booking before a confirmation is issued; a price change afterwards sends it back.
Four-eyes: nobody prices, authorises, issues or records payment on their own trip, the Director included.
Brokers set only enquiry, quoted, sent for authorisation or cancelled. Money stages are recorded by the Director, or a person the Director has mandated.
Every flight is followed to the last landing. The broker follows up within 24 hours and sends a rating request; a score of 3 or less starts service recovery.
Client ratings are quoted publicly only with the client's written consent. Never write, buy or reward reviews.
trouble: A client asks for our bank details
Never send them. The client pays through the payment request you create.
A client wants to fly in 3 days
Full payment is due at once, before the operator is paid. Create the payment request straight away.
You want to offer a client less than the 9% margin
Ask the Director first: any other margin is the Director's decision, with the reason recorded.
A client rates the trip 3 or lower
Start service recovery: call the client, find out what went wrong and tell the Director.
A happy client offers a review
Quote it publicly only with their written consent, and never reward reviews.
tips: If you are unsure about a rule, ask the co-pilot or Help before you send the trip for authorisation.
try: broker
Make a test enquiry with an operator price of USD 30,000 and check the client price: 30,000 ÷ 0.91, rounded up, is USD 32,968.

features.title: Client data and privacy
features.purpose: How we protect clients, contacts and the company.
steps: Real client details go only into real trips in the portal: never into training, the test version, the AI or messages outside the portal.
The AI co-pilot gets trip facts only, never passport, ID or bank numbers, passenger names or private contact details. Describe the trip, not the person.
Business contacts are hidden until you press Show, opening them is recorded, and contacts cannot be exported.
Every screen carries a watermark with your name, so screenshots are traceable.
We never talk about our clients, inside or outside the company.
trouble: A client sends passport copies by WhatsApp
Upload them to the trip in the portal, then delete them from your phone.
Someone asks who our clients are
We never name clients. Refer them to the Director.
tips: If you are unsure whether you may share something, don't: ask the Director first.

Add a contact only with a work email or work phone published by the organisation itself or taken from a licensed database, and give the source.
Your first message says where you found their details and offers an opt-out.
If someone opts out, press Opted out twice: their details are deleted from every list and nobody can add them again.
Press Contacted today after each contact. Contacts not reached within 12 months are deleted automatically.
trouble: Save contact says Work email only
Personal addresses like Gmail are not allowed. Use the work email or work phone.
It says This person has opted out
They asked not to be contacted. Nobody can add them again.
tips: Never use LinkedIn messages or bought lists to find people.
Organisations first: the company's general email is often the best first route.

features.title: Operators and service partners
features.purpose: The suppliers we can book worldwide: charter operators, and service partners in their own sections.
steps: Prospects, Operators: charter operators from the ARGUS and WYVERN audit registries (read every morning), the official certificate lists of the aviation authorities (the UK CAA list first; more authorities follow) and the research agent. Each shows its list or registry, audit level, certificate, fleet and sanctions pre-screen.

Filter operators by region, country, list or registry, audit level and Checks (Something to confirm / Nothing to confirm). Every operator shows what is still to confirm before the first booking: certificate and insurance for registry operators, insurance for those on an official list.

Prospects, Service partners: one section per function, never mixed. Aviation services (FBOs and ground handlers, trip support, in-flight catering) at business airports worldwide; Hotels (crew hotels, and hotels and resorts for our clients); Ground transport (limousine and chauffeur); Helicopters; Yachts.

Crew hotels are listed only if they are at most 15 minutes from the airport and have their own airport shuttle. Hotels and resorts for clients must show five-star or luxury standard on their own page or a recognised guide. Helicopter operators need an operator certificate; yacht charters are marked to confirm licence and insurance.
One record per company, with all its airports, contacts and routes. Airline ground handlers, airport companies, maintenance firms and software are not service partners.
Suppliers are never assigned to brokers as leads.

The research agent adds service partners every morning, airport by airport worldwide (141 business airports), each section with its own progress, then a refresh every 30 days. Each one is checked before it goes in.
trouble: An operator shows Possible sanctions match
Do not contact or book it. The Director decides.
An operator has no country yet
It came from a registry that lists only the name. The research agent completes about 25 a morning; filter Checks: Something to confirm.
An airport has no service partner for what you need
Add one with Add prospect and its public source, or ask the Director.
tips: Check IS-BAH for handlers and ARGUS or Wyvern for operators before relying on them.
Use List or registry: UK CAA AOC list to see operators whose certificate the authority itself lists.

features.title: Supplier quotes
features.purpose: Ask several suppliers at an airport for a quote, compare them on one screen and award one.

For each supplier, copy the prepared message, send it from your work email and press I have sent it.
Record each quote in USD, with how long it is valid and any changes to our terms.
Compare the scores and their reasons, then Award. Whoever made the request cannot award it, and a reason is needed if you do not choose the top score.
Add the awarded cost to the trip's direct trip costs.

It failed a check: opted out, possible sanctions match, sanctions check not run yet, or a crew hotel not shown within 15 minutes with a shuttle.
There is no Award button

features.title: Client signature
features.who: The Director, or a person the Director has mandated (never on their own trip); brokers see the status
features.purpose: Every issued confirmation is signed by the charterer before payment is recorded, and the signed copy is kept with the trip.
steps: After the confirmation is issued, the trip shows a Client signature panel: Not sent, Sent or Signed.

Check the charterer's email and press Send for signature. The confirmation PDF downloads and your mail program opens a ready-written email with the itinerary, price, payment schedule, how to sign and the payment-request-only warning. Attach the PDF and send it from the bookings mailbox. The trip is marked Sent at once.
When the signed PDF comes back, drop it on the panel. It saves to the trip straight away and is logged in the audit trail.
No answer after 24 hours: the button changes to Send a reminder.
Record client payment unlocks only after the signed contract is saved. A revision needs a new signature; the earlier signed copy stays in the file.

Your computer has no default mail program. Use Copy email text and paste it into webmail, then attach the downloaded PDF.
Record client payment is missing
The signed contract is not saved yet. Drop the signed PDF on the Client signature panel.
The charterer changed the PDF before signing
Do not accept it. Prepare a revision with the change, issue it and send the new version.
tips: Send the PDF the same hour it is issued.
Use the bookings mailbox for every send, never a personal account.

features.title: Cancelling a trip
features.who: Brokers cancel their own enquiries and quotes; after that the Director, or a person the Director has mandated
features.purpose: What happens when a client cancels, and what they pay.
steps: The client cancels in writing. The charge depends on how long before the first departure we receive the notice.
Scale, as a share of the charter price: more than 14 days 25%; 7 to 14 days 40%; 72 hours to under 7 days 65%; 24 to under 72 hours 85%; under 24 hours or no-show 100%.
The client pays the higher of the scale or the operator's own cancellation charge plus our fee. Each confirmation prints the charges for that booking.

Brokers can cancel their own trip while it is an enquiry or a quote. After that, the Director, or a person the Director has mandated, cancels it with Cancel trip; any refund is handled in the payment account.
trouble: The client cancels by phone
Ask them to confirm in writing: the time we receive it decides the charge.
The operator charges more than our scale

tips: Tell the client the cancellation charges before they sign.

faqIntro: The first 15 questions below were written before launch. From then on the FAQ grows from real questions: everyone can ask in the portal under Help, the AI answers at once, and questions asked often are added to the FAQ without names or client details. The Director reviews every entry. The live FAQ in the portal is always the current one.
faq: How is the client price calculated?
Operator all-in price plus direct trip costs, divided by 0.91 and rounded up. Archē's margin is 9% of the price the client pays. A lower margin needs the Director's approval.
When does the client pay?

25% of the charter price on signature, at least USD 2,500; the balance, including fixed-price extras, 7 calendar days before the first departure. If departure is less than 7 days away, the full price on signature. Items at cost are invoiced after the flight and paid within 10 calendar days.
What is the difference between a fixed-price extra and an extra at cost?

Fixed price: a supplier quoted it in writing before booking; the client pays the supplier price ÷ 0.91, rounded up, with the balance. At cost: the amount depends on the day (de-icing, extra parking, out-of-hours fees); it is invoiced after the flight with the receipt, without margin.
Why did my lead move to another broker?
No first contact was logged within 48 hours of assignment, or no follow-up within 14 days. The lead moves with its full history. Log every contact in the portal to keep your leads.
How many prospects must I add?
At least 10 organisations a month, each with the public source where you found it. Adding more earns points and a bigger share of new leads.
Do I get a fee for prospects I add?
No. Commission rewards the booking. Adding prospects earns points, a place on the leaderboard and a bigger share of new leads, and you work your own finds first.
Who issues the charter confirmation?

The Director, or a person the Director has mandated, after the operator price, KYC, sanctions screening and the payment request are done. Nobody checks, prices, approves, issues or records payment on their own trip.
The airport I want is not in the list. What do I do?
Type the four-letter ICAO code. The list holds airports suitable for jets; if it is still missing, ask the Director, because the runway may be too short.
Can a client pay by bank transfer to us directly?
No. Clients pay only through the payment request. Never send or accept bank details by email, chat or messaging apps.
Can I quote a domestic flight on a foreign aircraft?
No. Domestic legs on foreign-registered aircraft are cabotage and are refused in most countries. Use a local operator for the domestic leg or redesign the trip.
What does de-icing cost?
It depends on the day, the aircraft and the airport. Never give a figure: list it as an operational extra at cost, and pass on the operator's written estimate only as its estimate if the client asks.
Can a passenger bring a dog?
Only with the destination's entry rules met and the operator's written acceptance. Some countries accept pets only on approved routes and airports. Ask before quoting.
The client wants to change the trip after confirmation. What happens?
The Director gets the operator's new price in writing and issues a numbered revision. Changes to routing or passengers need new permits and may be refused; any difference is paid before the flight.
When is commission paid?
For trips that have flown and whose client payment has cleared, in the month of the flight, by the 15th of the next month.
Who sees my leads and trips?
You, the Director and any person the Director has mandated. Other brokers cannot see them. Client details stay in the portal; copying them is blocked.
How soon after a flight must I call the client?
Within 24 hours of the last landing. Log it in the trip's Aftercare panel; after 24 hours it shows as overdue on Today.
Can we publish a client's rating or comment?
Only with the client's written permission, recorded with the rating. We never write reviews ourselves or offer anything in return for a review.
What happens when a client rates 3 or less?
Service recovery: call the client within 1 working day, agree what happens and by when, and record it. The Director is told automatically.
Does the Roleplay lab score count for certification?
No. It is practice. Certification is decided by the Director's scored live lab (manual 14.4).
Will Archē pay for the ACA Air Charter Essentials course?

Proposed, not yet agreed: after you pass the written exam and 3 supervised bookings, Archē may pay the ACA directly, with a clawback if you leave within 12 months. See manual 14.1; if Archē decides to sponsor, the terms are set out in writing first.
Where is the portal course?
It is now Systems training in the Archē Broker Academy, after the written exam: one lesson per screen, each with a Try it task in the test version and a short check. Training in the portal opens it.
